# Vendored third-party code

Everything in this directory is someone else's code, committed into Nexley's own repo
on purpose, pinned to an exact version, and served from Nexley's own origin.

## Why this isn't a CDN link

Until 2026-09-08 `app.html` loaded supabase-js like this:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@supabase/supabase-js@2/dist/umd/supabase.min.js"></script>
```

That one line had five separate problems, and it was the **only** off-origin script on a
page that holds a signed-in student's session token in `localStorage` and their entire
notebook in IndexedDB. Anything executing there can read both.

1. **`@2` is a floating range, not a version.** jsDelivr resolved it to whatever the
   latest 2.x happened to be. On the day this was fixed jsDelivr was serving `2.115.0`
   while npm's `latest` was already `2.116.0` — so the version students were running was
   decided by a CDN cache expiry, not by anyone here. A new release would have started
   executing in signed-in sessions with no commit, no diff, no test run, and no way to
   tell after the fact which version any given user had loaded.

2. **No Subresource Integrity hash.** There was no `integrity=` attribute, so the browser
   would execute whatever bytes came back. A compromised CDN or a hijacked npm publish
   runs arbitrary JavaScript with full access to the session and the notes.

3. **The file was generated by the CDN, not published by Supabase.** This is the part that
   turns a theoretical risk into a concrete one. The npm package ships
   `dist/umd/supabase.js`. It does **not** contain `supabase.min.js` at all — jsDelivr
   minifies that file itself, on demand. So the exact artifact Nexley executed had no
   publisher-signed counterpart anywhere and there was nothing to verify it against.
   (It was also *larger* than the file Supabase actually publishes: 214,393 bytes vs
   214,101. The published UMD is already a production bundle.)

4. **The service worker precached it.** A bad version wouldn't just load once — it would
   be written into every user's cache and served from there until `CACHE` was bumped.

5. **It breaks the native wrap.** Phase 8 is a Capacitor build. Loading the core auth
   library over the network from a third party means the app can't cold-start offline,
   and shipping executable code that arrives from outside the bundle is the kind of thing
   App Review asks about.

Same-origin fixes all five at once. There is no CDN request, no SRI needed (it's our own
file), it works offline and inside the native wrap, and the version is a line in a diff.

Note that the web fonts under `app/fonts/` were already vendored for exactly this reason.
The CDN script was the one remaining exception, and the audit checklist in
`GROWTH_AND_LAUNCH.md` §11 had it recorded as *"Third-party embeds — N/A none currently"*,
which is how it stayed invisible.

## What's here

| File | Package | Version | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `supabase-js-2.115.0.js` | `@supabase/supabase-js` | 2.115.0 | npm registry tarball, `dist/umd/supabase.js` |

`supabase-js-2.115.0.js` is byte-for-byte `package/dist/umd/supabase.js` from
`supabase-js-2.115.0.tgz`, whose tarball hash was checked against the integrity value the
npm registry publishes for that version **before** anything was extracted:

```
sha512-PYJSxtCo37R7tTZW6pAqsxUeSx/dlhA7zn8RzKEUSCqyTxCUhG+iHrDTb04UyVBYbttaUbhwkNTvb8h5HW+uZA==
sha256 of the vendored file: f387e5935730a6d9599a281986a176eafce5ebbe7514446222d21aa029e31dd5
```

2.115.0 was chosen because it is precisely what jsDelivr was serving in production at the
moment of the change. This commit is a supply-chain fix and nothing else — no library
upgrade rode along with it. Moving to 2.116.0 is a separate, reviewable decision.

## How to update the version

Don't do this casually. It is the auth library.

```bash
V=2.116.0            # the version you actually intend to ship

# 1. Verify the tarball against the registry's own integrity hash BEFORE extracting.
curl -s "https://registry.npmjs.org/@supabase/supabase-js/${V}" > meta.json
TARBALL=$(node -p "require('./meta.json').dist.tarball")
EXPECTED=$(node -p "require('./meta.json').dist.integrity")
curl -sfL "$TARBALL" -o sb.tgz
ACTUAL="sha512-$(openssl dgst -sha512 -binary sb.tgz | openssl base64 -A)"
[ "$ACTUAL" = "$EXPECTED" ] || { echo "INTEGRITY FAIL — stop here"; exit 1; }

# 2. Extract the UMD build only.
tar xzf sb.tgz package/dist/umd/supabase.js
cp package/dist/umd/supabase.js "app/vendor/supabase-js-${V}.js"
git rm "app/vendor/supabase-js-<old version>.js"
```

Then update all three references — they are checked by `test/test_supplychain.js`, which
fails the build if they drift apart or if an off-origin `<script src>` ever reappears:

- the `<script src>` in `app/app.html`
- the `SHELL` entry in `app/sw.js` (and bump `CACHE` in the same edit, or returning users
  keep the old file)
- the table in this file

Finally, sign in on the live site and confirm the session survives a reload. A broken auth
library does not fail loudly — it fails as "everyone is logged out".
